title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft Grothendieck is axiomatising 'figures'. These are closed unions of strata in a stratified object whose set of strata M is partially ordered by incidence. The axiomatics also include an order or 'neighbourhood' relation ≪ (written ≼ in its weak form) and a notion of disjointness subject to a compatibility relation; the axioms are labelled C1–C7, with further 'Cont' axioms. On p.74 he stated a corollary: if K is a sub-figure of F with K ≠ F, there is a non-empty figure G disjoint from K but not from F. That is, a figure is determined by the figures disjoint from it. He then observed that this is not formal from C1–C4 alone.

On this page he finishes the counter-model. Take the degenerate model in which the set of figures is P_f(M), the closed (down-closed, Alexandrov-closed) subsets of the poset M. Disjointness means A∩B = ∅ with no further condition, since the compatibility relation is always true. Suppose M has a least element 0. Then every non-empty closed set contains 0, so the only figures disjoint from a non-empty F are empty, and the corollary fails.

In this model, axiom C6 for an order relation ≼ on P_f(M) reduces to: if F' ≼ F, then F' is empty iff F is. Taking ≼ to be the discrete order (equality), C6 and C7 hold tautologically. So C1–C7 do not imply the corollary, and an extra axiom is needed. He guesses it will be the implication '⇒' of axiom Cont 4 (p.35). A marginal addition seems to say that something also follows from C4 (cf. p.47), and that for now he should not use the hypothesis that ≪ is of a certain (illegible) kind.

A long crossed-out passage tries a direct argument. Strata Y ≪ X are considered, together with the boundary ∂X and strata Y' ≤ Y lying in ∂X. Then, for G ≪ F and a closed F' ≤ F, he considers the 'neighbourhood G' of F' induced by G' and wants G' = ∅ ⇔ G disjoint from F'.

He abandons this and concludes that the notion of induced neighbourhoods must be developed first. That is done on p.76: for G ≪ F and F' ≤ F there is a largest sub-figure G' of G with G' ≪ F'; it is the infimum of G and F' for ≪, and G' = ∅ ⇔ G disjoint from F' ('non évident').

The problem served is a combinatorial/order-theoretic axiomatics of stratified spaces and their regular (tubular) neighbourhoods, the 'tame topology' programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: No mathematical error in the surviving text. The counter-model is correct: with a least stratum, every non-empty closed set meets every other non-empty one, so the separation corollary fails while C6 and C7 hold for the discrete order.
The crossed-out attempt is incoherent and incomplete (abandoned mid-formula), which the author himself recognises by deferring to a theory of induced neighbourhoods.

ideas.what: Counter-model (closed sets of a poset with a least element, trivial compatibility, discrete order) showing that the separation corollary does not follow from axioms C1–C7
ideas.modern_name: independence proof via a model; Alexandrov topology on a finite poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard model-theoretic practice; Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies

ideas.what: Separation property: a figure is determined by the set of figures disjoint from it (to be secured by an extra axiom, the '⇒' part of Cont 4)
ideas.modern_name: separativity / disjunction property in a lattice of closed sets (cf. separative posets, T_D-type conditions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in lattice theory / locale theory

ideas.what: Induced neighbourhood: given a neighbourhood G ≪ F and a sub-figure F' ≤ F, the trace G' of G which is a neighbourhood of F', with G' = ∅ iff G is disjoint from F'
ideas.modern_name: restriction of regular / tubular neighbourhoods to closed unions of strata (Thom–Mather control data, regular neighbourhoods in PL topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data); Whitehead, Rourke–Sanderson (regular neighbourhoods)
ideas.where_published: Programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on 'topologie modérée'

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic, purely order-theoretic theory of figures with a neighbourhood relation ≪ (axioms C1–C7, Cont 1–7) for tame stratified spaces is left in draft. This page shows him testing the independence of the axioms and deciding he needs a theory of 'induced neighbourhoods' before he can prove basic separation properties. An abstract axiomatics of regular neighbourhoods of this kind does not seem to have been carried out in the literature in this form, though o-minimal and stratification theory cover the geometric content.
missed.quote: Il faut développer la notion de voisinages induits.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is part of the unrealised 'tame topology' foundation from the Esquisse. Relevant to exit-path categories / stratified homotopy theory, where an axiomatic neighbourhood calculus on strata posets could be compared with Lurie's and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka's frameworks. The page itself is only a working step, however.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine working page: a small counter-model showing axiom independence, and an abandoned attempt leading to the decision to develop induced neighbourhoods. Its interest lies only in documenting the unpublished axiomatic tame-topology programme, not in any new result on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'la relation d'être disjoints' should probably read 'la relation d'ordre discrète' (≼ = equality), which makes C6 and C7 tautological.
Margin: 'Aussi est-il [?] ... de C4 (vrai[?] p. 47)' appears to be 'Aussi est-il [inutile?] ... résulte de C4 (cf. p. 47)'.
Line 1: '(pour une relation d'ordre[?] ≼ sur F = P_f(M))' — 'd'ordre' is inserted above the line; the following word may be 'simple' or 'triple'.
Last line 'Cpactité[?] : voyons[?] des axiomes)' is likely 'Compatibilité : v. groupe des axiomes)' or similar; uncertain.
